thread:
evan_cust: hey team — we've got production customers complaining that streamed responses from the hosted API are truncating ~40% of the time. they see early EOF, and our billing shows those as 5xx. customer is asking for credits. here are two sample request ids: req_9ab3f2 and req_9ab3f8. timestamped around 2026-03-09T17:12:12Z and 17:18:03Z. can you advise? :grimacing:

alice_support: thanks for the heads up, evan. sorry about the disruption. can you paste one of the raw request headers and the curl you used? also does the client close the connection intentionally after partial data?

ev an_cust: here's the exact curl we used to stream the generation (we do chunked client-side):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \n  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?model=open-super
```
we're reading chunks and occasionally calling socket.close() if downstream user navigates away. we never got an explicit 4xx from you, just abrupt termination and our app shows the request was logged as 5xx.

alice_support: ok that's useful. @ben_sre i'm escalating, attaching the request ids. logs show gateway had "write: broken pipe" for those request ids. can you take a look at classification logic?

ben_sre: looking. initial grep for req_9ab3f2 shows gateway: `error=EPIPE write_failed upstream_write` and then `response_code=502` in access log. full snippet: 
```
[2026-03-09T17:12:12Z] req=req_9ab3f2 method=POST path=/v1/stream upstream=runtime-12 write_err=EPIPE response_code=502 latency=0.34s
```
That looks like the gateway attempted to write to the downstream socket, got EPIPE, and our classification mapped it into 5xx. we treat most upstream write errors as server failures.

carla_platform: flagging design note — for streaming, downstream client aborts (socket close) should be treated differently: not a server error. nginx uses 499 for client closed request. counting those as 5xx causes false incident signals and billing disputes.

ben_sre: i can reproduce locally. quick repro using python to open the stream and close after receiving a chunk: 
```python
import requests, time, socket
s = requests.Session()
r = s.post('https://local-gateway:8443/v1/stream', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer X','Accept':'text/event-stream'}, stream=True)
for i, chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=None)):
    print('got', i)
    if i==0:
        r.close()  # client abort
        break
```
Gateway logs: `write() returned EPIPE` on the next write to downstream. current code path marks this as backend failure.

ben_sre: proposed change: detect EPIPE / ECONNRESET on write to downstream and classify as client_abort (internal tag: client_disconnect) instead of 5xx. Also we should not increment the 5xx counter or bill the tokens for that request.

carla_platform: agree. also add metric `gateway.client_disconnect` and set access-log field `client_disconnect=true` so downstream billing and analytics can exclude them. we need a short patch and a canary.

alice_support: for the customer: do we have a rollback/backfill plan for billing credits? evan, we should proactively offer credits for the affected request ids until this is resolved.

ev an_cust: yes please — they want credits for the affected sessions. they estimate ~120 truncated streams across the org this week.

ben_sre: here's a minimal patch sketch (pseudocode) for gateway classification: 
```diff
- if (upstream_write_failed) { classify_as_5xx(); }
+ if (upstream_write_failed) {
+   if (errno == EPIPE || errno == ECONNRESET) {
+      // downstream closed socket; treat as client abort
+      log_tag('client_disconnect');
+      classify_as_499(); // or internal non-5xx sentinel
+      metrics.increment('gateway.client_disconnect');
+   } else {
+      classify_as_5xx();
+   }
+ }
```
note: we use 499 as audit-friendly label but we actually map it to a non-billing outcome in billing pipeline.

carla_platform: please include unit tests that simulate partial writes and assert classification. also add an integration test with nginx-like client abort. we should also ensure the streaming runtime does not swallow the original EPIPE and convert it to a different error code upstream.

ben_sre: onboarding checklist for canary: 
- add logs at info level for first 1h in canary (req id, errno, classification)
- deploy to canary region with 1% traffic
- monitor gateway.client_disconnect metric and 5xx rate
- validate billing pipeline excludes client_disconnect-tagged requests
I'll open a PR in eng-runtime and eng-platform.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for gateway@canary-2026-03-10T02:20Z (traffic=1%). :rocket:

alice_support: internal next actions for support: 
- reply to customer: apologize, tell them we see EPIPE on the gateway for the provided request ids, classify those as client disconnects, and we're issuing credits for the affected requests.
- ask for any additional request ids they want us to check (we'll run a quick filter).
- follow up when canary completes and when permanent fix lands.

ev an_cust: appreciated. pls send me the credits confirmation and an ETA for a permanent fix.

ben_sre: ETA: canary tonight, full rollout in 48-72h if no regressions. i'll attach PR when ready.

carla_platform: also FYI — add a flag to billing: `exclude_client_disconnect=true` and backfill script to find matching access-log entries between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-10. we'll coordinate accounting.

alice_support: TL;DR for customer message draft: 
"Hi Evan — thanks for reporting. we traced the truncations to downstream client disconnects (EPIPE) at our gateway that were being misclassified as 5xx. we've put a canary patch in place to classify these as client_disconnect (non-billing). we'll issue credits for the affected request ids you provided and follow up when the fix is fully rolled out (ETA 48–72h). — Alice" :white_check_mark:

ben_sre: added note to PR: also ensure we don't give false positives for server-side crashes where we legitimately retried and failed. classification must check if upstream actually acknowledged completion or not.

alice_support: perfect. evan — we'll send the customer the credits confirmation and keep this thread updated. thanks everyone :pray:

deploy-bot: canary complete — no regressions observed in initial 2h. traffic=1%. monitoring: 5xx_rate down 0.6% in the canary cluster, gateway.client_disconnect=45 (first 2h).

ben_sre: rolling to 10% now, will watch logs.

alice_support: marking this case high priority and creating billing ticket to backfill credits. closing loop with the customer after full rollout.

ev an_cust: thanks all — appreciate quick turnaround. :wave:
